newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne to make statement Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne to make statement Thursday.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne said on Wednesday it had requested a trading halt in its ordinary and converting preference shares because it was considering a confidential proposal, the terms of which had not been concluded.
It said it would make an announcement on Thursday.
"The board is currently considering a confidential proposal, the terms of which have not been concluded, and an announcement will be made tomorrow," Bank of Melbourne said in a statement.
Earlier on Wednesday Bank of Melbourne's shares jumped 65 cents to A$8.80 on volume of 155,012 shares.
Bank of Melbourne is widely seen as a potential takeover target
St George Bank Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp have been tipped by analysts as possible suitors for the Melbourne-based bank.

But Treasurer Peter Costello, who must approve any bank merger, said last week that he did not expect any merger application while the goverment was still considering the official Wallis Inquiry into the financial system.
Costello is due to release the Wallis report next week. The report is widely expected to recommend the relaxation of big bank merger rules.

However, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) which regulates anti-monopolies laws, has said it would not allow a bank merger that left a state banking market without at least one regional bank.
Bank of Melbourne is the last major regional bank in Victoria. Its last chief executive, David Airey, resigned in January and has yet to be replaced.
